subject: white bellbird
title: The Loudest Bird on Earth Blasts Its Song Into Its Date's Face

scenes.text: The loudest bird on Earth weighs half a pound.
The white bellbird, from the northern Amazon. Its call peaks at 125 decibels.
That's louder than a jackhammer, with three times the sound pressure of the old record holder.
Here's the strange part. He saves his loudest song for when a female lands right beside him.
Then he swivels and blasts the final note straight into her face.
A song as loud as a pile driver, delivered from one perch away.

description:
The white bellbird of the northern Amazon has the loudest call ever recorded from a bird: 125 decibels, about three times the sound pressure of the previous record holder, the screaming piha.
The bird weighs only about a quarter of a kilogram. Males sing their loudest song when a female perches right next to them, swivelling to deliver the final note directly at her. Jeff Podos and Mario Cohn-Haft published the measurements in Current Biology in 2019.
Would you stay for the second note? Comment below.
first_comment: It has unusually thick abdominal muscles to power that call. What is the loudest animal you have ever heard?
